proofs.proof_tex:
Let \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{eq}}\) denote, only within this proof, the subfamily of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cert}}^{(q)}(K,J)\) for which every observed alphabet has cardinality \(q\).  Positive latent support gives, for every \(k\) and \(r\in\mathcal Q\),
\[
 P(H_k=r)=\sum_{h_{-k}\in\mathcal Q^{K-1}}\pi_{(r,h_{-k})}>0.
\]
Consequently \(\lvert\operatorname{supp}(H_k)\rvert=q\).

We next verify the asserted support statement for a selected observed coordinate.  Fix \(j=s(a,k)\).  By the definition of the certificate, all factors \(c_{a,k,u}\) are nonnegative and all their exponents are positive.  Since a member of \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{eq}}\) satisfies \(\Delta_{mathrm{DT}}\ne0\), every such factor is nonzero.  In the equal-alphabet case, Definition~\textnormal{def:local-minors} and Theorem~\textnormal{thm:local-factorization} give
\[
 c_{a,k,u}=\det(B_{a,k,u})^2>0.
\]
Thus \(B_{a,k,u}\) is invertible.  For any \(x\in\mathcal Q\), its row indexed by \(x\) cannot be zero, so there is an \(r\in\mathcal Q\) with
\[
 L_{a,k,u}(x,r)>0.
\]
The event \(H_{\rho_a(1:k-1)}=u, H_{\rho_a(k)}=r\) has positive probability by positive latent support.  The definition of \(L_{a,k,u}\) therefore yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P(X_j=x)
 &\ge
 P\!\left(H_{\rho_a(1:k-1)}=u,
           H_{\rho_a(k)}=r\right)
 L_{a,k,u}(x,r)\\
 &>0.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Because the alphabet itself has exactly \(q\) states, this proves \(\lvert\operatorname{supp}(X_j)\rvert=q\) for every selected row.  More generally every observed variable in \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{eq}}\) is discrete and has support cardinality at most \(q\).

Lemma~\textnormal{lem:chen-mixed-sufficient-measurement} records that a discrete sufficient measurement in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Chen}}\) must have support strictly larger than that of its latent parent and that every latent-parent set must have two such measurements.  In \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{eq}}\), the latent-parent support has cardinality \(q\), whereas every observed support has cardinality at most \(q\).  Hence no observed variable in this subfamily can satisfy that strict support inequality, and the two-sufficient-measurement requirement fails.

The equal-alphabet certified subfamily is nonempty.  Proposition~\textnormal{prop:ternary-witness}, using Lemma~\textnormal{lem:positive-faithful-parameters-dense}, produces a faithful rational perturbation on the displayed graph \(\Gamma^{\star}\) with ternary observed alphabets and \(\Delta_{\mathrm{DT}}>0\).  It belongs to \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{eq}}\), but the preceding support argument excludes it from \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Chen}}\).  Thus \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{eq}}\not\subseteq\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Chen}}\).

For the reverse noncontainment, Lemma~\textnormal{lem:chen-mixed-sufficient-measurement} states that the mixed class permits continuous sufficient measurements and multifactor measurement graphs without the two-disjoint-triangular-view restriction.  Any admissible member having a continuous observed coordinate is outside \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{eq}}\), because every observed coordinate in \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{eq}}\) has a finite \(q\)-point alphabet.  Hence \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Chen}}\not\subseteq\mathcal C_{\mathrm{eq}}\), proving incomparability.

Finally, the same cited lemma states that Chen et al.'s completeness condition supplies a discretization with a full-rank conditional table.  In contrast, in the present subfamily full rank follows algebraically from \(\Delta_{mathrm{DT}}\ne0\): Theorem~\textnormal{thm:local-factorization} gives full column rank of both triangular-view matrices, and Theorem~\textnormal{thm:certificate-frontier} makes this equivalent to the nonvanishing local determinants in the equal-alphabet case.  Thus the two rank mechanisms asserted in the statement are distinct, and all parts of the narrowed claim follow.

Write \(C_k=\operatorname{ch}_X(H_k)\) for the observed-child set of the \(k\)-th latent coordinate.  Reading the columns of \(\Gamma^{\star}\) gives
\[
 C_1=\{1,2,3,5,6,7\},\qquad
 C_2=\{2,3,4,5,6,8\},\qquad
 C_3=\{3,6,7,8\}.
\]
For each ordered pair of distinct sets, the differences are nonempty: for example, \(1\in C_1\setminus C_2\), \(4\in C_2\setminus C_1\), \(1\in C_1\setminus C_3\), \(8\in C_3\setminus C_1\), \(2\in C_2\setminus C_3\), and \(7\in C_3\setminus C_2\).  Hence no one of these child sets contains another.

Rows \(1,2,3\) have diagonal parents \(1,2,3\), respectively, in the order \((1,2,3)\), and none has a parent later than its diagonal parent in that order.  Rows \(4,5,6\) have diagonal parents \(2,1,3\), respectively, in the order \((2,1,3)\), with the same zero pattern for later parents.  This proves double triangularity for the displayed \(S_1,S_2,\rho_1,\rho_2\).  In \(S_3=\{7,8\}\), row \(7\) is a child of latent coordinates \(1,3\), while row \(8\) is a child of coordinates \(2,3\); thus every latent coordinate has an \(S_3\)-child.  Every child \(3,6,7,8\) of \(H_3\) has at least two latent parents, so \(H_3\) has no pure child.

For a fixed observed row \(j\), the displayed conditional probabilities are normalized because, for every \(h_\ell\in\{0,1,2\}\),
\[
 \sum_{x=0}^{2}
 \left(\mathbf 1\{x=h_\ell\}-\frac13\right)=0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \sum_{\ell:\,\Gamma^{\star}_{j\ell}=1}c^{\star}_{j\ell}
 \le 2^{-(4+j)}\sum_{\ell=1}^{3}8^{-\ell}
 <\frac1{224}.
\]
Since \(-1/3\le \mathbf 1\{x=h_\ell\}-1/3\le2/3\), every measurement-table entry lies in the interval
\[
 \left(\frac13-\frac1{3\cdot224},
       \frac13+\frac2{3\cdot224}\right)\subset(0,1).
\]
Combining these tables by conditional independence across the observed coordinates with the independent uniform latent law gives the Markov factorization for the graph with empty latent DAG.  All latent weights and all measurement-table entries are strictly positive, so the resulting complete-data law \(P^{\star}\) is strictly positive.

To prove measurement nondegeneracy, fix \(j\) and two different configurations \(h,h'\) of its latent parents.  Let \(\ell_0\) be the smallest parent index for which \(h_{\ell_0}\ne h'_{\ell_0}\), and evaluate the difference of the two conditional mass functions at \(x=h_{\ell_0}\).  Terms with index smaller than \(\ell_0\) cancel, the \(\ell_0\)-term equals \(c^{\star}_{j\ell_0}\), and the remaining terms have total absolute value at most
\[
 \sum_{\substack{\ell>\ell_0\\
                   \Gamma^{\star}_{j\ell}=1}}
 c^{\star}_{j\ell}
 <c^{\star}_{j\ell_0}
   \sum_{r=1}^{\infty}8^{-r}
 =\frac17c^{\star}_{j\ell_0}.
\]
The evaluated difference is therefore nonzero.  Thus distinct parent configurations induce distinct conditional distributions.

Because the latent coordinates are independent, conditioning on a predecessor context does not change the distribution of any later latent coordinate.  Separating the diagonal-parent term in each selected measurement table consequently gives
\[
 B_{a,k,u}
 =b^{\star}_{s(a,k),u}\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}
  +c^{\star}_{s(a,k),\rho_a(k)}Q_3.
\]
Set \(t=c^{\star}_{s(a,k),\rho_a(k)}\) and \(b=b^{\star}_{s(a,k),u}\).  Since \(\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}b=1\), the decomposition
\[
 \mathbb R^3=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf 1\}
 \oplus\{v:\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}v=0\}
\]
shows that \(Bv=tv\) on the two-dimensional zero-sum subspace, while
\[
 B\mathbf 1=3b
 =\mathbf 1+3\left(b-\frac13\mathbf 1\right).
\]
In a basis adapted to this decomposition, \(B\) is block triangular with diagonal entries \(1,t,t\).  Therefore
\[
 \det(B_{a,k,u})=t^2
 =\left(c^{\star}_{s(a,k),\rho_a(k)}\right)^2>0.
\]
Definition~\textnormal{def:certificate} then gives \(\Delta_{mathrm{DT}}>0\).

Strict positivity is a finite collection of strict inequalities.  Measurement nondegeneracy is also witnessed by finitely many strict inequalities between table columns, and the certificate condition is witnessed by finitely many nonzero determinants.  These properties therefore persist in a relatively open neighborhood \(U\) of the displayed table parameter; the graph properties persist because the graph is fixed.  By Lemma~\textnormal{lem:positive-faithful-parameters-dense}, the faithful positive Markov parameters are dense and relatively open, so every nonempty relative open subset of \(U\) meets that set in a nonempty relative open set.  Rational simplex coordinates are dense in the affine product of table simplices.  Hence every such neighborhood contains a rational parameter that is faithful and retains all the preceding strict properties.  Its induced joint law is rational because the Markov factorization uses only finite sums and products of rational table entries.

Every rational law so obtained satisfies all member properties in Definition~\textnormal{def:certified-class}, and hence belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cert}}^{(3)}(3,8)\).  Theorem~\textnormal{thm:fixed-k-identification} then identifies its quotient recovery target from its observed law.  The already verified child sets and the absence of a pure child of \(H_3\) are unchanged.  This proves every assertion, without requiring the particular displayed parameter \(P^{\star}\) itself to be faithful.

Let \(V\) be the finite vertex set of \(G\).  Use \(q-1\) free coordinates in each conditional probability vector, with the final coordinate equal to one minus their sum, and write \(\theta\) for the resulting point in the affine product of conditional-table simplices.  The strict parameter space is the relative interior \(\Theta^{+}\) of that product.  By the Markov factorization, every joint cell probability is a polynomial in \(\theta\): explicitly,
\[
 P_{\theta}(z)=
 \prod_{i\in V}
 \theta_i\!\left(z_i\mid z_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)}\right),
\]
after the final entries have been replaced by their affine expressions.  Every marginal cell probability is therefore a finite sum of such polynomials.

Fix distinct vertices \(i,j\), a conditioning set \(C\subseteq V\setminus\{i,j\}\), states \(r,r',s,s'\in\mathcal Q\), and \(c\in\mathcal Q^C\).  Define the cross-product polynomial
\[
 F_{r,r',s,s',c}(\theta)
 =P_{\theta}(r,s,c)P_{\theta}(r',s',c)
  -P_{\theta}(r,s',c)P_{\theta}(r',s,c).
\]
Strict positivity ensures \(P_{\theta}(C=c)>0\).  Hence
\[
 Z_i\mathrel{\perp}Z_j\mid Z_C
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 F_{r,r',s,s',c}(\theta)=0
 \quad\text{for all }r,r',s,s',c.
\]

Suppose now that \(i\) and \(j\) are d-connected given \(C\).  We show that at least one polynomial in the preceding collection is not the zero polynomial.  Choose an active path and split it at its collider vertices into collider-free sections.  On the boundary of the binary submodel using states \(0,1\), assign an independent fair bit \(Z_t\) to each section.  A collider-free section has at most one fork, so its arrows point away from a source along each of its two arms; set every vertex on that section to copy \(Z_t\) along those arrows.  If the collider between adjacent sections carries bits \(Z_{t-1},Z_t\), set its value to
\[
 D_t=Z_{t-1}\oplus Z_t,
\]
where \(\oplus\) denotes addition modulo two.  Activity of the path says that this collider itself, or one of its descendants, belongs to \(C\).  Transmit \(D_t\) along a directed path to such a conditioned vertex.  When transmission paths meet, take the modulo-two sum of their incoming signals and transmit the resulting parity to one common reachable conditioned vertex; when they branch, retain one branch and set unused conditioned vertices constantly equal to zero.  Thus the transmitted collider parities are partitioned into groups, and conditioning the selected vertices in \(C\) to zero imposes
\[
 \bigoplus_{t\in I_g}D_t=0
 \quad\text{for every group }I_g.
\]
All vertices and arrows not used by this path gadget are made constant or ignored by their children.  These are legitimate deterministic conditional tables and hence define a boundary point of the Markov parameter polytope.

Taking the modulo-two sum of the displayed group equations uses every collider parity once and gives
\[
 0=\bigoplus_tD_t
  =\bigoplus_t(Z_{t-1}\oplus Z_t)
  =Z_0\oplus Z_T.
\]
The endpoint variables therefore agree on a conditioning configuration \(c_0\) having positive probability.  Both endpoint values occur with positive probability, because \(Z_0\) is fair, while the two discordant endpoint cells have probability zero.  Consequently, at this boundary parameter,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &P(0,0,c_0)P(1,1,c_0)
  -P(0,1,c_0)P(1,0,c_0)\\
 &\hspace{4em}=P(0,0,c_0)P(1,1,c_0)>0.
 \end{aligned}
\]
For \(q>2\), the same construction simply assigns zero mass to the unused states.  Mixing every deterministic conditional table with an arbitrarily small uniform \(q\)-state table produces a point of \(\Theta^{+}\).  The displayed strict inequality persists for all sufficiently small mixtures by continuity.  Thus one cross-product polynomial associated with every d-connected triple \((i,j,C)\) is genuinely nonzero on the affine parameter space.

There are finitely many triples \((i,j,C)\).  For each d-connected triple choose one nonzero polynomial \(F_{i,j,C}\) as above.  If a Markov parameter is unfaithful, some conditional independence not entailed by d-separation holds.  Choosing a d-connected vertex pair from the two conditionally independent sets shows that this parameter belongs to the zero set of the corresponding \(F_{i,j,C}\).  Hence the unfaithful set is contained in
\[
 \bigcup_{(i,j,C)}\{\theta:F_{i,j,C}(\theta)=0\}.
\]

For completeness, a nonzero polynomial on a finite-dimensional real affine space has a zero set of Lebesgue measure zero and empty interior.  This follows by induction on the dimension: in one dimension there are finitely many roots; in higher dimension, write the polynomial as a polynomial in the last coordinate, apply the induction hypothesis to the common zero set of its nonzero coefficient polynomials, and apply one-dimensional finiteness on every remaining fiber.  Finite union preserves nullity and empty interior.  The preceding union is therefore relatively null and nowhere dense in \(\Theta^{+}\).  Its complement is dense and has full relative Lebesgue measure.

Finally, for a fixed d-connected triple, dependence is the condition that at least one of its finitely many cross-product polynomials is nonzero, which is relatively open.  Intersecting these open conditions over the finitely many d-connected triples shows that the faithful set is relatively open.  The Markov factorization supplies every conditional independence entailed by d-separation, so absence of any additional conditional independence is exactly faithfulness.  The faithful positive parameters are therefore relatively open, dense, and of full Lebesgue measure in the affine product of simplex interiors, as claimed.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
The equal-alphabet subfamily of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cert}}^{(q)}(K,J)\), consisting of models in which every observed coordinate has alphabet cardinality \(q\), and \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Chen}}\) are incomparable in the ambient mixed-type latent-structure universe.  Within this equal-alphabet subfamily, every selected observed variable has support cardinality \(q\), so Chen et al.'s discrete sufficient-measurement requirement
\[
 \lvert\operatorname{supp}(X_j)\rvert>
 \lvert\operatorname{supp}(H_k)\rvert
\]
cannot hold when the relevant latent coordinate has support cardinality \(q\); the dense ternary witness is therefore outside their two-sufficient-measurement class.  Conversely, \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Chen}}\) permits continuous measurements and graphs without two disjoint triangular views, so it is not contained in the equal-alphabet certified subfamily.  Completeness in Chen et al. supplies a discretization with full-rank tables, whereas this project derives full rank from the finite local certificate without assuming completeness or larger-support measurements.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current certified class allows heterogeneous observed alphabets of cardinality at least q. Its assertion that every selected observed support has cardinality q is therefore false outside the equal-alphabet subfamily. The proposal explicitly restricts only the new certified side of the comparison and leaves the published Chen class unchanged.

proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(\mathcal L=\mathscr L(P_X)\).  Membership of \((G,P)\) in
\(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cert}}^{(q)}(K,J)\), by
Definition~\textnormal{def:certified-class}, entails in particular the
measurement-graph restriction, the Markov factorization, positive latent
support, measurement nondegeneracy, third-view coverage, the subset
condition, and faithfulness.  It also entails
\(\Delta_{\mathrm{DT}}\ne0\), so
Theorem~\textnormal{thm:certificate-frontier} gives
\(\operatorname{rank}(M_1)=\operatorname{rank}(M_2)=q^K\).  The premise of
the present theorem supplies the exact component output: a set
\(\mathcal L\) of \(q^K\) labels and the conditional distribution of each
\(X_j\) in each component, all under one common but unknown permutation of
\(\mathcal Q^K\).

For \(j\in\{1,\ldots,J\}\), define the true latent parent-index set
\[
 A_j=\{k\in\{1,\ldots,K\}:\Gamma_{jk}=1\}.
\]
Fix any bijection \(\psi:\mathcal L\to\mathcal Q^K\) matching the recovered
components to the true latent configurations; such a bijection exists by
the assumed exact component recovery.  Positive latent support guarantees
that every configuration has positive mixing weight, so all conditional
columns used below are defined.  The Markov factorization and the
measurement-graph restriction imply, for every \(h\in\mathcal Q^K\),
\[
 P(X_j=\,\cdot\mid H=h)
 =P(X_j=\,\cdot\mid H_{A_j}=h_{A_j}).
\]
Consequently, if \(h_{A_j}=h'_{A_j}\), the two conditional columns for
\(X_j\) agree.  Conversely, measurement nondegeneracy says that two
distinct configurations of \(H_{A_j}\) induce distinct conditional
distributions.  Thus the observable relation \(E_j\), pulled through
\(\psi\), is exactly
\[
 E_{A_j},\qquad
 h\mathrel{E_A}h' \Longleftrightarrow\ h_A=h'_A
 \quad(A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,K\}).                                      \tag{1}
\]

Order equivalence relations by inclusion as subsets of
\(\mathcal Q^K\times\mathcal Q^K\), and let \(\wedge\) and \(\vee\)
denote their meet and join.  Directly from (1), for all
\(A,B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,K\}\),
\[
 E_A\wedge E_B=E_{A\cup B},
 \qquad
 E_A\vee E_B=E_{A\cap B}.                                               \tag{2}
\]
The first equality is intersection of the two relations.  For the second,
both \(E_A\) and \(E_B\) are contained in \(E_{A\cap B}\), proving one
inclusion.  If \(h\mathrel{E_{A\cap B}}h'\), choose
\(z\in\mathcal Q^K\) by setting \(z_A=h_A\), \(z_B=h'_B\), and assigning
arbitrary states off \(A\cup B\).  The assignments agree on
\(A\cap B\), so they are consistent, and
\(h\mathrel{E_A}z\mathrel{E_B}h'\).  Hence the equivalence relation
generated by \(E_A\cup E_B\) contains \((h,h')\), proving the reverse
inclusion.

Let
\[
 C_k=\{j:k\in A_j\}=\operatorname{ch}_X(H_k).
\]
Third-view coverage makes every \(C_k\) nonempty.  If \(\ell\ne k\), the
subset condition gives \(C_k\not\subseteq C_\ell\); hence some
\(j\in C_k\setminus C_\ell\) contains \(k\) but not \(\ell\) in its
parent set.  It follows that
\[
 \bigcap_{j\in C_k}A_j=\{k\},
 \qquad
 E_{\{k\}}=\bigvee_{j\in C_k}E_j,                                      \tag{3}
\]
where the second equality follows from (2).  Thus every one-coordinate
relation occurs in the finite lattice generated observably by the
\(E_j\)'s.

Moreover, \(E_A\) has exactly \(q^{|A|}\) equivalence classes: its classes
are indexed by the possible values in \(\mathcal Q^A\).  Induction using
(2) shows that every relation in the lattice generated by the \(E_j\)'s is
some \(E_A\).  Since \(q\ge3\), such a relation has exactly \(q\) classes
if and only if \(|A|=1\).  In conjunction with (3), this gives the entirely
observable characterization
\[
 \{E_{\{1\}},\ldots,E_{\{K\}}\}
 =\{F:F\text{ belongs to the generated lattice and has exactly }q
       \text{ classes}\}.                                               \tag{4}
\]

Enumerate the relations in (4) as \(F_1,\ldots,F_K\), and, for each
\(k\), choose a bijection
\(\lambda_k:\mathcal L/F_k\to\mathcal Q\).  Define
\[
 \varphi_{\mathrm{coord}}(\ell)
 =\bigl(\lambda_1([\ell]_{F_1}),\ldots,
          \lambda_K([\ell]_{F_K})\bigr).                                \tag{5}
\]
The meet of the relations in (4) is
\(E_{\{1,\ldots,K\}}\), which is equality on \(\mathcal L\).  Therefore
(5) is injective.  Its domain and codomain each have \(q^K\) elements, so
it is bijective.  The only choices in (5) are the ordering of the \(K\)
relations and the naming of the \(q\) classes of each relation.  These are
exactly a coordinate permutation and an independent state permutation in
each coordinate, namely the action of
\(\mathfrak G=\mathfrak S_K\ltimes(\mathfrak S_q)^K\).  Hence the
coordinate alignment is unique modulo \(\mathfrak G\).

It remains to recover the advertised structure after this alignment.  For
every \(j,k\), equation (1) gives
\[
 k\in A_j\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad E_j\subseteq E_{\{k\}}.           \tag{6}
\]
Indeed, the forward implication follows because agreement on \(A_j\)
implies agreement on coordinate \(k\).  If \(k\notin A_j\), choose two
configurations agreeing on \(A_j\) and differing at \(k\); then the pair
belongs to \(E_j\) but not to \(E_{\{k\}}\), proving the converse.
Formula (6) is an observable recovery map for every row of \(\Gamma\).
Transporting each recovered conditional column through (5) gives
\(p_j(\cdot\mid h)=P(X_j=\,\cdot\mid H=h)\) for all \(j,h\).  The Markov
factorization also gives conditional independence of the observed
coordinates given \(H\), so these columns determine the aligned matrix
\[
 M_1(x,h)=\prod_{j\in S_1}p_j(x_j\mid h).
\]
Let \(v_1\) be the observable probability vector of \(X_{S_1}\), in the
same row order as \(M_1\).  Marginalizing the latent variable gives
\(v_1=M_1\pi\).  Since \(M_1\) has column rank \(q^K\), its Gram matrix is
invertible and hence
\[
 \pi=(M_1^{\mathsf T}M_1)^{-1}M_1^{\mathsf T}v_1.                        \tag{7}
\]
Thus the weights are recovered from \(P_X\), rather than assumed as part of
the decomposition output.  The true weights satisfy (7), and positive
latent support makes every entry strictly positive.  The recovered
\(\Gamma,\pi,p\) are unique subject to the same \(\mathfrak G\)-action.

Finally, the recovered strictly positive table \(\pi\) determines every
latent conditional-independence statement by finite marginalization.  In
particular, every conditioning event in a latent configuration has positive
probability, so the requisite conditional probabilities involve no division
by zero.  For latent vertices and latent conditioning sets, d-separation in
\(G\) is the same as d-separation in \(\Lambda\): by the measurement-graph
restriction, any observed vertex internal to a path between latent vertices
is a sink and hence a collider, and it has no descendants; a path with such
an internal vertex is therefore blocked when conditioning only on latent
vertices.  The remaining paths are precisely the paths in \(\Lambda\),
with unchanged collider status.  Faithfulness of \(P(H,X)\) to \(G\) now
implies that the conditional-independence model computed from \(\pi\) is
exactly the d-separation model of \(\Lambda\).

For completeness, this last recovery is finite and explicit: enumerate all
DAGs on the \(K\) aligned latent vertices and retain those whose
d-separation relations equal the recovered latent conditional-independence
relations.  The true \(\Lambda\) is retained by faithfulness, and
Lemma~\textnormal{lem:dag-markov-equivalence-characterization} says that
all retained DAGs, and only they, have the same skeleton and unshielded
colliders as \(\Lambda\).  They therefore form exactly
\([\Lambda]_{\mathrm{MEC}}\).  Equations (4)--(7), transport of the
conditional columns, and this finite DAG enumeration recover
\([\Gamma,\pi,p,[\Lambda]_{\mathrm{MEC}}]_{\sim}\), proving the claim.
